ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a circle, with a point on the lower left of the circumference. From this point two chords are drawn, respectively connecting to the point marked G on the upper right of the circle and the point marked H on the right side of the circle. The inscribed angle formed by the two chords at the lower-left point on the circumference is marked as 28°. What is sought is the degree measure of arc GH. Reasoning: This 28° angle is an inscribed angle intercepting arc GH. According to the inscribed angle theorem, the degree measure of an inscribed angle is equal to half the degree measure of its intercepted arc, so the degree measure of arc GH is equal to 2 × 28° = 56°.

Use the inscribed angle theorem: an inscribed angle measures half of its intercepted arc. Therefore m arc GH = 2 × 28 = 56.
